mainTopic: Sharing in communal suffering, divine judgment, and whether fasting is a sin or holy
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a discussion about why a traveler should eat little on the road. The גמרא shows when the 'stomach' reason and the 'food supply' reason give different results, and it tells us what רב פפא did and why. Next come teachings about famine years. רב says that someone who holds back from eating in a famine is saved from an unusual death. ריש לקיש says couples may not have relations in famine years, and a ברייתא adds that those with no children yet may. ברייתות then teach that a person must share the צבור's suffering, as משה did when he sat on a stone, and must never separate himself or party privately. They also describe who testifies against a person who sinned in secret, and they explain the fairness of ה׳'s judgment from 'אל אמונה ואין עול צדיק וישר הוא'. Finally the גמרא returns to fasting. שמואל says one who fasts is called a חוטא, and רבי אלעזר says he is called קדוש; both learn this from the נזיר. The גמרא then begins to question whether רבי אלעזר really holds this, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When the two reasons give different results
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers what the practical difference is between the 'stomach' reason and the 'food supply' reason. The first case is a traveler sitting in a boat. The second is a traveler going from station to station.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is when he sits in a boat. Or else, when he travels from one station to the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question it just asked: what is the real difference between the two reasons for not eating too much on the road? It gives two cases where the reasons split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A boat ride involves no hard physical effort, so the stomach worry falls away, but food could still run out. Going from station to station means you can buy more food along the way, so the food worry falls away, but the bumpy road can still upset the stomach. Each case knocks out one reason while keeping the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A station or inn along the road where travelers stop
The bowels or stomach (the digestion reason)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the boat case and the station case are two separate rules. They are two examples of the same thing: a situation where only one of the two reasons applies, so the two opinions would rule differently.

phrases.english: Where he is sitting in a boat.
phrases.notes: This answers the question just before it: when would the 'stomach' reason and the 'food' reason make a difference?

phrases.english: Or else, where he travels from station to station.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'מאי בינייהו', which came just before this section, about the two reasons for eating little on the road.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference is there between the stomach reason and the food-supply reason?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On a boat only the food reason applies. Going station to station only the stomach reason applies.

steps.title: What רב פפא did on the road
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא ate one loaf of bread for every פרסה he traveled. He held that the reason for the rule is the stomach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא would eat one loaf of bread for every single פרסה he traveled. He held that the rule is because of the stomach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how רב פפא acted when traveling. It explains that his behavior fits the opinion that the rule is about the stomach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry were running out of food, eating along the way would be a problem. Since רב פפא held the worry is digestion, eating a little at a time while traveling did not bother him. His practice shows which of the two reasons he followed.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of distance, roughly four 'מיל'
He holds (this explains the reasoning behind someone's view or action)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa, for each and every parasang,
would eat one loaf of bread.
He held that it is because of the bowels.
phrases.notes: This is the 'stomach' reason from step 1, not the 'food supply' reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא כׇּל פַּרְסָה וּפַרְסָה אָכֵיל חֲדָא רִיפְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows an אמורא acting according to one of the two reasons discussed in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא held the rule is about the stomach, so he ate small amounts regularly while traveling.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for eating little on the road: the stomach and the food supply. They split in the boat case and the station case, and רב פפא followed the stomach reason.

steps.title: Holding back from food in a famine saves from an unusual death
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says in the name of רב that someone who keeps himself hungry during famine years is saved from an unusual death. He brings a פסוק from איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: anyone who makes himself go hungry in years of famine will be saved from an unusual death, as it says: 'In famine He redeemed you from death.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about famine years. Someone who eats less during a famine is rewarded by being saved from a strange death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, connected to the earlier discussion of famine and of eating less. The idea is that a person who has food but still eats less, sharing in the community's suffering, earns a special reward. The proof from the פסוק is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Anyone who starves himself in years of famine
is saved from an unusual death,
as it is stated: "In famine He redeemed you from death."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב כׇּל הַמַּרְעִיב עַצְמוֹ בִּשְׁנֵי רְעָבוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about famine years, moving on from the travel discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who keeps himself hungry during a famine is saved from an unusual death.

steps.title: How the פסוק teaches this: 'in famine' instead of 'from famine'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the פסוק should have said 'from famine'. Since it says 'in famine', it means that because of the famine (his own hunger), he is saved from death.
steps.simpleTranslation: It should have said 'from famine.' Rather, this is what it means: as a reward for starving himself in years of famine, he is saved from an unusual death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק proves רב's teaching by looking closely at one word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain reading would expect 'He saves you from famine.' The word 'בָּרָעָב' ('in' or 'through' famine) suggests the famine itself is the reason for being saved. So holding himself back from food during the famine is what earns him rescue from death.

keyTerms.meaning: It should have said; it needed to say
Rather, this is what it is saying

phrases.english: It should have said "from famine"!
Rather, this is what it is saying:
As a reward for starving himself in years of famine,
he is saved from an unusual death.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵרָעָב מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ אֶלָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 3 supports רב's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רב's teaching that one who keeps himself hungry in a famine is saved from an unusual death.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The unusual wording 'בָּרָעָב' instead of 'מֵרָעָב' in איוב 5:20.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the פסוק as simply promising rescue from hunger. The גמרא's point is that the hunger is the reason for the reward, not the danger he is rescued from.

steps.title: No marital relations during famine years
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says a person may not have marital relations in years of famine. He learns this from יוסף, whose sons were born before the famine began.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: a person is forbidden to have marital relations in years of famine, as it says: 'And to יוסף were born two sons before the year of famine came.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another famine-years teaching, this time a prohibition on marital relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה stresses that יוסף's sons were born before the famine. ריש לקיש reads this as showing that יוסף did not have children during the famine. He concludes that people should not have relations during such years.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: אָסוּר לְאָדָם לְשַׁמֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ בִּשְׁנֵי רְעָבוֹן,
phrases.english: It is forbidden for a person to have marital relations in years of famine,
as it is stated: "And to Joseph were born two sons
before the year of famine came."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָסוּר לְאָדָם לְשַׁמֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ בִּשְׁנֵי רְעָבוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second teaching about how to behave during famine years, alongside step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marital relations are forbidden during famine years.

steps.title: Exception: couples without children
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that couples who do not yet have children may have relations even in famine years.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: those without children may have marital relations in years of famine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that limits ריש לקיש's rule. Couples who have no children are not included in the ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's prohibition does not apply to everyone. People who have not yet had children still need to fulfill the מצוה of having children, so they are allowed. The rule stays in place for everyone else.

phrases.english: It was taught: those lacking children
may have marital relations in years of famine.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא חֲסוּכֵי בָּנִים מְשַׁמְּשִׁין מִטּוֹתֵיהֶן בִּשְׁנֵי רְעָבוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the prohibition in step 5 by giving an exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Couples without children may have relations even during famine years.
steps.whatToRemember: In famine years, someone who eats less is rewarded with rescue from an unusual death. Marital relations are forbidden then, except for couples who have no children yet.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the famine restriction is limited and gives way to the מצוה of having children.

steps.title: The angels' curse on one who separates from the community
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when ישראל is suffering and one person separates himself, his two accompanying מלאכים declare that he will not see the נחמה of the צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: When the Jewish people are in distress and one of them separates himself, the two ministering angels who accompany every person come, place their hands on his head, and say: 'This man who separated himself from the community, let him not see the community's comfort.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a person who cuts himself off from the community's suffering. It tells us the heavenly consequence he faces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps spoke about holding back from food and relations in famine years. This ברייתא gives the reason behind that behavior: a person must not separate himself from the צבור when it suffers. The punishment fits the sin. He cut himself off from their pain, so he is cut off from their comfort.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
When the Jewish people are immersed in distress
and one of them separates himself,
two ministering angels come
who accompany a person,
and they place their hands on his head,
and they say: This so-and-so
who separated himself from the community
let him not see the comfort of the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל שְׁרוּיִין בְּצַעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the broader principle behind the famine-year behaviors of steps 3–6: do not separate from the suffering צבור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who separates himself from the suffering צבור will not see the נחמה of the צבור.

steps.title: Do not say 'I will go home and eat and drink'
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא forbids enjoying oneself privately while the צבור suffers. It applies the פסוק in ישעיהו, whose next verse says such a sin is not forgiven until death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: When the community is suffering, a person should not say, 'I'll go home, eat and drink, and all is well with me.' If he does, the verse speaks about him: 'Behold joy and gladness, slaughtering cattle and sheep, eating meat and drinking wine; eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.' And the next verse says: 'ה׳ of hosts revealed in my ears: this sin will not be forgiven you until you die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא with the same message. It describes a person who ignores the community's pain and goes home to enjoy himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא described the heavenly result. This one describes the actual behavior and gives a פסוק as the source. The proof comes from what follows the פסוק: the sin of carefree eating during a crisis is so serious that it is not atoned for until death.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in another ברייתא
Peace be upon you, my soul (all is fine with me)

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
When the community is immersed in suffering,
a person should not say: I will go to my home,
and I will eat and drink,
and peace be upon you, my soul.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם עוֹשֶׂה כֵּן — עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And if he does so, the verse speaks about him:
"And behold joy and gladness,
slaying oxen and slaughtering sheep,
eating meat and drinking wine;
eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die."
What is written right after it?
"And the Lord of hosts revealed Himself in my ears:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יְכֻפַּר הֶעָוֹן הַזֶּה לָכֶם עַד תְּמֻתוּן״.
phrases.english: surely this sin will not be forgiven for you until you die."
phrases.notes: Here the word אִם works like an oath and means 'it will surely not.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר שָׁרוּי בְּצַעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא making the same point, now with a פסוק and a concrete description of the forbidden behavior.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During communal suffering one may not indulge in private eating and drinking; such a sin is not forgiven until death.

steps.title: The worse level: the wicked who hope tomorrow will be the same
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא calls the previous case the level of בינונים. It then quotes a harsher פסוק describing רשעים, whose result is that the צדיק is taken away before the coming evil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to here is the way of in-between people. But about the way of wicked people, what is written? 'Come, I'll get wine and we'll fill up on strong drink, and tomorrow will be just like today.' And what is written after it? 'The righteous one perishes and no one takes it to heart, that the righteous one is taken away because of the evil to come.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and separates two levels of bad behavior. It brings a new פסוק for the worse level, the רשעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בינוני only says 'tomorrow we may die,' so he enjoys himself today while the crisis lasts. The רשע wants the party to continue and hopes tomorrow will be just like today. The result is even more severe: the צדיק is taken from the world so he will not see the punishment that is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: The righteous one is gathered (taken away from the world)

steps.confusionAlert: The בינונים here are not good people. They also sinned by partying during the crisis. The ברייתא only means their sin is less severe than that of the רשעים.

phrases.english: Up to here is the way of in-between people.
But regarding the way of wicked people, what is written?
"Come, I will get wine,
and we will fill ourselves with strong drink,
and tomorrow will be like this day."
What is written right after it?
"The righteous one perishes,
and no one takes it to heart,
that the righteous one is taken away because of the evil to come."

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן מִידַּת בֵּינוֹנִים. אֲבָל בְּמִדַּת רְשָׁעִים, מָה כְּתִיב?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the previous פסוק at the level of בינונים and adds a second, harsher level for רשעים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who wish for the indulgence to continue are רשעים, and their behavior brings the removal of the צדיק before the coming evil.

steps.title: The proper way: sharing the pain, as משה did
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the positive rule that a person should share the צבור's distress. It proves this from משה, who sat on a stone during the war with עמלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a person should share in the distress of the community. We find this with משה רבינו, who shared the community's distress, as it says: 'משה's hands were heavy, so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: After showing what not to do, the ברייתא now teaches what a person should do. It brings a פסוק about משה as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא turns from the bad examples to the correct behavior. The proof rests on a small detail in the פסוק: משה sat on a stone. This step sets up the question in the next step, which explains why that detail proves the point.

keyTerms.meaning: A person should share in distress with the community

phrases.english: Rather, a person should share in distress with the community,
for so we find with Moshe our teacher
that he caused himself distress together with the community,
as it is said: "And Moshe's hands were heavy,
phrases.notes: שמות 17:12, during the war with עמלק.

phrases.english: and they took a stone and put it under him,
and he sat on it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, יְצַעֵר אָדָם עִם הַצִּבּוּר, שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the negative examples to the positive obligation and brings a proof.
steps.raayaObject: The obligation to share in the צבור's distress.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 17:12: משה sat on a stone during the war with עמלק.

steps.title: Did משה really have nothing softer to sit on?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why משה sat on a hard stone. Surely he had a pillow or cushion.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't משה have even one pillow or one cushion to sit on?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a pointed question about the פסוק. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question shows that sitting on a stone was not a matter of having no choice. Since משה could easily have had a cushion, the stone must have been a deliberate choice. That is what makes the פסוק a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it so that...? (introduces a question with surprise)

phrases.english: But did Moshe not have
one pillow or one cushion
to sit on?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לֹא הָיָה לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה כַּר אֶחָד אוֹ כֶּסֶת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the detail in the פסוק from step 10 to show that it was intentional.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did משה sit on a stone when a pillow or cushion was surely available?

steps.title: משה chose to suffer along with ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The answer: משה said that since ישראל was suffering, he too would be with them in suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what משה said: Since the Jewish people are in distress, I too will be with them in distress.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. משה sat on the stone on purpose, to share the people's hardship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was not fighting on the battlefield. Even so, he found a way to feel some of their discomfort instead of staying comfortable. This completes the proof that a person should share the צבור's suffering.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what Moshe said:
Since the Jewish people are immersed in distress,
I too will be with them in distress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 and completes the proof from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה deliberately chose the stone to share in ישראל's suffering.

steps.title: The reward: seeing the community's comfort
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that whoever shares the צבור's distress merits seeing the נחמה of the צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anyone who shares in the distress of the community merits to see the comfort of the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes with the reward for sharing in the community's pain. It is the exact opposite of the punishment in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said that one who separates himself will not see the community's comfort. Here, one who joins in their pain will see it. The section is framed by these two matching ideas.
steps.whatToRemember: In a time of communal trouble, a person must not separate himself or enjoy himself privately. Whoever separates himself will not see the נחמה of the צבור. Whoever shares the pain, like משה on the stone, merits to see it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core idea behind the earlier rules about holding back in famine years: a Jew's personal conduct must reflect solidarity with the suffering צבור.

phrases.english: And anyone who causes himself distress together with the community
merits and sees the comfort of the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the lesson from משה with a general reward, mirroring the punishment in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One who shares the community's suffering merits to see its consolation.

steps.title: Who could testify against me?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא imagines a person who thinks his sins are hidden and asks: who will testify against me?
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe a person will say: Who will testify against me?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a question a person might ask: if I sinned where nobody saw, who could testify against me? This is a setup line, and the answers come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps spoke about judging how a person behaves toward the צבור. Here the ברייתא blocks the excuse that nobody saw. The question is not really asking for information. It sets up the point that nothing is truly hidden.

phrases.english: And lest a person say:
Who will testify against me?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's theme of judgment by heading off the excuse that a sin was hidden.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who will testify against a person who sinned in secret?

steps.title: The stones and beams of his house testify
steps.stepSummary: The first answer: the stones and beams of a person's own house testify against him, based on a פסוק in חבקוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The stones of a person's house and the beams of a person's house testify against him, as it says: 'For a stone will cry out from the wall, and a beam from the wood will answer it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. The very walls and beams of the person's house will testify against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer picks the place where a person feels most private: his own home. The פסוק describes a stone and a beam calling out, and the ברייתא reads this as the house itself speaking as a witness.

phrases.english: The stones of a person's house
and the beams of a person's house
testify against him, as it is stated:
"For a stone shall cry out from the wall,
and a beam out of the timber shall answer it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם וְקוֹרוֹת בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מְעִידִים בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The stones and beams of a person's house testify against him.

steps.title: The school of רבי שילא: the two angels testify
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי שילא say that the two מלאכי השרת who go with every person are the ones who testify against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי שילא say: The two ministering angels who accompany a person testify against him, as it says: 'For He will command His angels for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion gives a different witness. The two angels who always go with a person will testify about what he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer used objects in the house. This answer uses angels, who go with the person everywhere and not only at home. The פסוק shows that ה׳ assigns angels to each person, so they see everything he does.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study house) of רבי שילא

phrases.english: In the school of Rabbi Sheila they say:
The two ministering angels
who accompany a person,
they testify against him, as it is stated:
"For He will give His angels charge over you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two accompanying מלאכי השרת testify against a person.

steps.title: רבי חידקא: a person's own soul testifies
steps.stepSummary: רבי חידקא says a person's own נשמה testifies against him, based on a פסוק in מיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חידקא says: A person's soul testifies against him, as it says: 'From the one who lies in your bosom, guard the doors of your mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion says the witness is inside the person: his own נשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answers keep moving closer to the person: first his house, then the angels beside him, now his soul. רבי חידקא reads 'the one who lies in your bosom' as the נשמה, which knows everything a person does.

keyTerms.meaning: The one lying in your bosom

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥidka says:

phrases.aramaic: נִשְׁמָתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם הִיא מְעִידָה עָלָיו,
phrases.english: A person's soul testifies against him,
as it is stated: "From her who lies in your bosom
keep the doors of your mouth."
phrases.notes: מיכה 7:5. 'Her who lies in your bosom' is read here as the soul inside you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question of step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's own נשמה testifies against him.

steps.title: Some say: a person's own limbs testify
steps.stepSummary: A final opinion (יש אומרים) says a person's own limbs testify against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: A person's limbs testify against him, as it says: 'You are My witnesses, says ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth opinion says the person's own body parts, the very limbs that did the sin, will testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is the closest of all: the witness is the body itself. The פסוק 'You are My witnesses' is read as the person himself, meaning his own limbs, standing as witness.
steps.whatToRemember: Four answers to 'who testifies against me?': the house, the two angels, the soul, the limbs. They all make one point: no sin is truly hidden.

phrases.english: And some say:
A person's limbs testify against him,
as it is stated: "You are My witnesses, says the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and final answer to the question of step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's own limbs testify against him.

steps.title: 'A God of faithfulness': צדיקים pay for small sins in this world
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains 'אל אמונה'. Just as רשעים are punished in עולם הבא even for a small sin, צדיקים are punished in עולם הזה for a small sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A God of faithfulness and without wrong.' 'A God of faithfulness': just as the wicked are punished in the World to Come even for a light sin they do, so the righteous are punished in this world for a light sin they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא quotes a פסוק about ה׳'s justice and explains its first half. It shows that צדיקים are also held to account for small sins, but they pay for them in עולם הזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא now moves from witnesses to how the judgment is carried out. 'Faithfulness' means ה׳ lets no sin go unpaid, even a small one. The difference is only where the payment happens. רשעים pay in עולם הבא, and צדיקים pay in עולם הזה.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean צדיקים are judged more harshly. Every small sin is accounted for, and the צדיק simply pays for his in עולם הזה.

phrases.english: "A God of faithfulness and without iniquity."
"A God of faithfulness":

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנִּפְרָעִין מִן הָרְשָׁעִים לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
phrases.english: just as punishment is exacted from the wicked in the World to Come
even for a light transgression that they commit,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ נִפְרָעִין מִן הַצַּדִּיקִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: so too, punishment is exacted from the righteous in this world
for a light transgression that they commit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who testifies at judgment to how the judgment is carried out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ collects for every small sin: from רשעים in עולם הבא and from צדיקים in עולם הזה.

steps.title: 'And without wrong': רשעים get paid for small מצוות in this world
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains 'ואין עול'. Just as צדיקים are rewarded in עולם הבא even for a small מצוה, רשעים are rewarded in עולם הזה even for a small מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And without wrong': just as reward is paid to the righteous in the World to Come even for a light מצוה they do, so reward is paid to the wicked in this world even for a light מצוה they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the second half of the פסוק. Even רשעים get full reward for their small מצוות, but they are paid in עולם הזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of step 19. 'Without wrong' means ה׳ never withholds reward, even from a רשע. Together the two halves explain why we can see צדיקים suffer and רשעים succeed in עולם הזה.
steps.whatToRemember: The two halves of the פסוק mirror each other. צדיקים pay for small sins here and are rewarded there. רשעים are rewarded for small מצוות here and pay there. Nothing is missed, and nothing is unfair.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a classic answer to the question of why good people suffer and bad people prosper in this world.

phrases.english: "And without iniquity":

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּשַׁלְּמִין שָׂכָר לַצַּדִּיקִים לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
phrases.english: just as reward is paid to the righteous in the World to Come
even for a minor מצוה that they fulfill,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ מְשַׁלְּמִין שָׂכָר לָרְשָׁעִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: so too, reward is paid to the wicked in this world
even for a minor מצוה that they fulfill.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין עָוֶל, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּשַׁלְּמִין שָׂכָר לַצַּדִּיקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the פסוק with the reward side, mirroring step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ pays reward for every small מצוה: to צדיקים in עולם הבא and to רשעים in עולם הזה.

steps.title: At death a person sees his deeds and signs on them
steps.stepSummary: Explaining 'צדיק וישר הוא': when a person dies, all his deeds are listed before him, he confirms them, and he signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He is just and righteous.' They said: when a person leaves this world for his eternal home, all his deeds are laid out before him in detail. They tell him: you did this and that, in this place, on this day. He says: yes. They tell him: sign! And he signs. As the פסוק says: 'By the hand of every man He will seal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains the last part of the פסוק, 'צדיק וישר הוא'. When a person dies, his deeds are listed for him, he admits them, and he signs his name to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 19-20 explained 'אל אמונה' and 'ואין עול'. Now 'צדיק וישר הוא' teaches that God's judgment is fully fair. The person himself confirms every detail and signs, so nobody can say the judgment was wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: His eternal home, the next world
Listed one by one, in detail
Sign! (an order to sign one's name)

phrases.english: "He is just and righteous"
phrases.notes: דברים 32:4, the end of the same פסוק the earlier steps were explaining.

phrases.english: They said: at the time a person passes away
to his eternal home
all his deeds are listed in detail before him,
and they say to him: such and such you did
in such a place, on such a day,
and he says: yes,
and they say to him: sign! And he signs.
As it is said: "By the hand of every man He will seal."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's line-by-line reading of the same פסוק, now explaining its third part.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At death a person sees all his deeds, confirms them, and signs on them, as 'ביד כל אדם יחתום' says.

steps.title: The person agrees the judgment was fair
steps.stepSummary: Beyond signing, the person declares that he was judged well, fulfilling 'למען תצדק בדברך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, he also accepts the judgment as fair and tells them: you judged me well. This fulfills the פסוק: 'So that You will be justified when You speak.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more step. The person does more than sign; he openly says the judgment was right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Signing only shows the facts are true. Saying 'יפה דנתוני' goes further: the person agrees the verdict itself is just. This shows God is completely right, which is the point of 'צדיק וישר הוא'.

keyTerms.meaning: Accepts the judgment on himself as fair
To fulfill what the פסוק says

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא read 'אל אמונה ואין עול צדיק וישר הוא' piece by piece. Its point: God's judgment is completely fair, and at death the person himself admits it.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁמַּצְדִּיק עָלָיו אֶת הַדִּין,
phrases.english: And not only that, but he accepts the judgment on himself as just,
and he says to them: you have judged me well,
to fulfill what is said:
"So that You will be justified when You speak."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁמַּצְדִּיק עָלָיו אֶת הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further stage to step 21: after signing, the person also declares the judgment fair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person declares 'יפה דנתוני', showing God's judgment is just.

steps.title: שמואל: one who fasts is called a sinner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to fasting. שמואל says anyone who fasts is called a חוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: anyone who fasts is called a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main subject of the מסכתא, fasts. שמואל makes a strong statement: someone who fasts is called a חוטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, separate from the אגדה about judgment. שמואל's idea is that taking on suffering you don't need is wrong. The next step shows where he gets this from.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeping a fast (literally 'sitting in a fast')

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל הַיּוֹשֵׁב בְּתַעֲנִית נִקְרָא חוֹטֵא.
phrases.english: שמואל said: whoever sits in a fast is called a sinner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל כׇּל הַיּוֹשֵׁב בְּתַעֲנִית נִקְרָא חוֹטֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה about judgment and returns to the topic of fasting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who fasts is called a חוטא.

steps.title: שמואל's source: the נזיר is called a sinner
steps.stepSummary: שמואל follows רבי אלעזר הקפר, who reads 'מאשר חטא על הנפש' as saying the נזיר sinned by causing himself pain by holding back from wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds like this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר הקפר ברבי says, what does the פסוק mean, 'and he will atone for him for having sinned regarding the soul'? Against which soul did this person sin? Rather, he made himself suffer by holding back from wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל's view matches a תנא. רבי אלעזר הקפר asks how a נזיר 'sinned', and answers that he caused himself pain by giving up wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a נזיר says he needs atonement for sinning 'על הנפש'. Since he did nothing wrong to anyone, the sin must be the suffering he put himself through by giving up wine. This is the basis for calling self-denial a sin.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק coming to teach?
A person who vows to stay away from wine and some other things

phrases.english: He holds like this תנא,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר בְּרַבִּי אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: as it was taught: רבי אלעזר הקפר ברבי says:
phrases.notes: ברבי is a title of honor for a great scholar.

phrases.english: What does the פסוק come to teach when it says:
"And he will atone for him for having sinned regarding the soul"?
Against which soul did this one sin?
Rather, he made himself suffer by holding back from wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the תנאי source behind שמואל's statement.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's statement that one who fasts is called a חוטא
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר הקפר's reading of 'מאשר חטא על הנפש' about the נזיר

steps.title: From the נזיר to the one who fasts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with a קל וחומר: if the נזיר who gave up only wine is a sinner, then one who gives up everything is surely a sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a קל וחומר? If this person, who only held back from wine, is called a sinner, then someone who holds back from every single thing is surely one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר הקפר finishes his ברייתא by applying the נזיר to a person who fasts, using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר gives up one thing, wine, and is still called a sinner. A person who fasts gives up all food and drink, so his suffering is greater. That is exactly why שמואל calls him a חוטא.

keyTerms.meaning: Reasoning from a lighter case to a stronger one

phrases.english: And isn't this a קל וחומר?
If this one, who did not make himself suffer
except from wine,
is called a sinner,
then one who makes himself suffer by giving up each and every thing,
how much more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by extending the נזיר's 'sin' to one who fasts.
steps.raayaObject: That one who fasts is called a חוטא
steps.raayaSupportSource: קל וחומר from the נזיר, who gave up only wine

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: one who fasts is called holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the opposite: the נזיר is called קדוש, so one who fasts from everything is surely קדוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: he is called holy, as the פסוק says: 'He shall be holy, letting the hair of his head grow long.' If this person, who held back from only one thing, is called holy, then someone who holds back from everything is surely holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the opposite opinion. He uses the same נזיר and the same kind of קל וחומר, but he builds on the פסוק that calls the נזיר קדוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions start from the נזיר. רבי אלעזר הקפר focuses on 'חטא על הנפש' and concludes the faster is a sinner. רבי אלעזר focuses on 'קדוש יהיה' and concludes the faster is holy.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר here is a different person from רבי אלעזר הקפר in step 24. They hold opposite views.
steps.whatToRemember: Two opposite views on fasting, both drawn from the נזיר. רבי אלעזר הקפר and שמואל say one who fasts is a חוטא. רבי אלעזר says he is קדוש.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: נִקְרָא קָדוֹשׁ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר:
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר says: he is called holy, as it is said:
"He shall be holy, letting the hair of his head grow long."
If this one, who did not make himself suffer
except from one thing,
is called holy,
then one who makes himself suffer by giving up everything,
how much more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite opinion, using the same נזיר and the same kind of קל וחומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who fasts is called קדוש, by a קל וחומר from the נזיר who is called קדוש.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל: The נזיר is called holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to שמואל, who calls a faster a חוטא, what about the פסוק that calls the נזיר קדוש?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל, the נזיר is called holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל with the פסוק that רבי אלעזר used. If the נזיר is called קדוש, how can holding back from pleasure be a sin?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל built his view on the נזיר being called a חוטא. But the תורה also calls the נזיר קדוש, which seems to praise his holding back. So שמואל must explain that word.

phrases.english: And according to Shmuel,
but he is called holy!
phrases.notes: 'He' is the נזיר. This is the פסוק רבי אלעזר used in Step 26.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי אלעזר's proof from Step 26 to challenge שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that one who fasts is a חוטא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה calls the נזיר קדוש. That seems to praise holding back, not condemn it.

steps.title: The holiness is about his hair
steps.stepSummary: Answer for שמואל: the word קדוש goes on the growing of the נזיר's hair, not on the נזיר himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word refers to the growing of the locks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל. The word 'holy' describes the נזיר's growing hair, not the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק reads 'קדוש יהיה גדל פרע', so 'holy' can be joined to the hair growth. That way the תורה is not praising his holding back from wine, and שמואל's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The growing of the locks (the נזיר's uncut hair)

phrases.english: That refers to the growing of the locks.
phrases.notes: The פסוק is במדבר 6:5: 'he shall be holy, letting the locks of his hair grow.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what the פסוק refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קדוש praises the נזיר himself for holding back.
steps.terutzMaskana: קדוש describes only his growing hair, so it is not a proof against שמואל.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי אלעזר: The נזיר is called a sinner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around: according to רבי אלעזר, what about the פסוק that calls the נזיר a חוטא?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי אלעזר, the נזיר is called a sinner!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר with the פסוק שמואל used. If the נזיר is called a חוטא, how can holding back be holy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors Step 27. Each side has to deal with the other side's פסוק. Now רבי אלעזר must explain 'מאשר חטא על הנפש'.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Elazar,
but he is called a sinner!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of Step 27, now aimed at רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's view that one who fasts is קדוש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה says the נזיר 'sinned against the soul'. That seems to condemn holding back.

steps.title: The sin is becoming טמא
steps.stepSummary: Answer for רבי אלעזר: the 'sin' is about a נזיר who made himself טמא from a dead body, not about holding back from wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: That refers to a נזיר who made himself impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי אלעזר. The word 'sinned' is said about a נזיר who became טמא, which is forbidden to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the sin offering comes in the section about a נזיר who became טמא from a dead body. So the 'sin' is that טומאה, not his holding back from wine. This leaves רבי אלעזר's view standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity from contact with a dead body

steps.whatToRemember: Each side reads the 'other' פסוק narrowly: for שמואל, 'holy' is about the hair. For רבי אלעזר, 'sinned' is about the נזיר who became טמא.

phrases.english: That is one who made himself impure.
phrases.notes: He means a נזיר who touched a dead body, which a נזיר may not do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what the פסוק refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'חטא' condemns the נזיר's holding back from wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חטא' is about a נזיר who became טמא, so it is not a proof against רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: Did רבי אלעזר really say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new challenge. It brings another statement of רבי אלעזר that may clash with his praise of fasting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And did רבי אלעזר really say this? But didn't רבי אלעזר say: A person should always consider himself...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. It questions whether רבי אלעזר really holds that fasting is holy, and starts quoting another statement of his. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ומי אמר... הכי? והאמר...' is the classic way the גמרא shows that one אמורא seems to contradict himself. We only see the opening words of his other statement here. The full clash becomes clear when the quote is finished on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say this? (opens a self-contradiction challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: The quote is cut off in the middle. Don't try to work out the contradiction yet. Wait until the full statement of רבי אלעזר appears.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Elazar say this?
phrases.notes: 'This' means his view from Step 26 that one who fasts is holy.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
A person should always consider himself
phrases.notes: Literally 'measure himself.' The sentence is finished on the next part of the daf.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי אלעזר's reading of the פסוק, the גמרא now checks whether his view fits his other statements.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's statement that one who fasts is קדוש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another statement of רבי אלעזר seems to point the other way. The details come when the quote is finished.
